title: Stopped for a breath test (drink-driving)
triggers: police asking me to take a breath test
peeke gaadi chala raha tha police ne pakda

rights.plain_explanation: Driving with more than 30 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood, as measured by a breath analyser, is an offence. A first offence can mean up to six months in jail, a ₹10,000 fine, or both.
A police officer in uniform can ask you for a breath test if they suspect drink-driving. If you refuse and they suspect alcohol, they may arrest you without a warrant.
For drink-driving, police may seize your licence to send for disqualification, with a written acknowledgement.

do_now: Cooperate with the breath test; refusing makes it worse.
Don't drive any further. Ask a sober friend, or use a cab.
Ask for the official challan and an acknowledgement if your licence is taken.
If you're arrested, your arrest rights apply: ask for the grounds and tell a family member.
user_at_fault_cases: If you drove after drinking above the limit, the law is against you. The challan, licence seizure and court case are lawful. Sage won't help you avoid or beat a breath test.

escalation.label: Free legal aid
escalation.detail: Call NALSA on 15100 or visit your District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) at the district court. Women, children, people in custody and people below the income limit get a free lawyer.
